description: We are an enthusiastic and mission-driven team stepping into the NASA Space Apps challenge, blending real-world space mission data with interactive design and engineering.
summary: GALAXY RUN – Mission Beyond Earth is an interactive space exploration game inspired by the Google Chrome Dinosaur game. It replaces the dinosaur with a futuristic spaceship travelling through space. Players must avoid obstacles such as asteroids, fireballs, meteor showers, solar flares, and space debris while exploring a visually attractive universe containing planets, stars, and galaxies.The game combines arcade gameplay with basic space engineering concepts. Players can design their spacecraft by selecting rockets, fuel capacity, scientific instruments, power systems, and communication equipment. Each selection affects spacecraft mass, power, fuel, communication, and budget. Players must manage limited resources and make effective engineering decisions.The game features three missions: Moon Exploration, Mars Exploration, and Asteroid Exploration. During gameplay, players encounter challenges such as power shortages, communication failures, and asteroid fields. Their decisions influence mission performance and success.The project incorporates scientific information from official NASA educational resources, including facts about Ceres, Vesta, and Bennu, without using NASA branding or logos.Developed using Python and Pygame, GALAXY RUN aims to make space exploration and engineering concepts educational, interactive, and enjoyable.
details:
GALAXY RUN – MISSION BEYOND EARTH

1. What does your project do or how does it work?

GALAXY RUN is an interactive space exploration and mission simulation game inspired by the Google Chrome Dinosaur game. Instead of a dinosaur, players control a futuristic spaceship travelling through space. Players must avoid obstacles such as asteroids, fireballs, meteor showers, and space debris. The game also includes spacecraft design, mission selection, fuel management, power management, scientific instruments, and communication systems. Players make engineering decisions to complete missions to the Moon, Mars, and asteroids successfully.

2. What benefits does your project have?

The project makes learning about space exploration and engineering more interesting and interactive. It helps students understand spacecraft design, resource management, scientific instruments, orbital challenges, and mission planning. It also develops problem-solving, critical-thinking, and decision-making skills through gameplay.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our main aim is to make complex space engineering concepts easier for students to understand through an enjoyable gaming experience. The project encourages curiosity about astronomy, space technology, and scientific exploration. It demonstrates how engineering decisions and limited resources influence the success of real-world space missions.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Language: Python.
  • Game Development Library: Pygame.
  • Development Environment: Google AntiGravity.
  • Deployment Platform: Vercel (for the browser-compatible version).
  • Scientific References: Official NASA educational resources.
  • Hardware: A computer or laptop for development and gameplay.

5. How is your project creative?

The creativity of GALAXY RUN comes from combining an endless-runner arcade game with space mission simulation. Instead of simply avoiding obstacles, players must also manage spacecraft resources, select scientific equipment, and make important engineering decisions. The space-themed environment, animated obstacles, interactive missions, and real astronomical facts create an educational gaming experience.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered several important factors while designing the project:

  • Mission objectives: Different goals for Moon, Mars, and asteroid exploration.
  • Budget: Keeping spacecraft development within limited credits.
  • Mass: Ensuring the spacecraft does not exceed its mass limit.
  • Fuel: Maintaining sufficient fuel for the journey.
  • Power: Managing energy for spacecraft operations and scientific instruments.
  • Communication: Maintaining contact with the spacecraft.
  • Safety: Avoiding asteroids and other space hazards.
  • Scientific accuracy: Using educational information from official NASA resources.
  • User experience: Making the game attractive, simple, interactive, and enjoyable.

Overall, GALAXY RUN demonstrates how gaming can make space science and engineering education more engaging while helping students understand the importance of planning, resource management, and effective decision-making.
